ranked_evidence.title: Yogi Adityanath
ranked_evidence.snippet: # Yogi Adityanath. A member of the Bharatiya Janata Party, Adityanath has served as the chief minister of Uttar Pradesh since 2017. | Member "Member of the Legislative Assembly (India)") of Uttar Pradesh Legislative Assembly |. | **In office** 18 September 2017 – 22 March 2022 |. In 2017, he moved from central to the UP state politics and was elected as the chief minister of Uttar Pradesh. Yogi Adityanath was born as Ajay Mohan Singh Bisht on 5 June 1972 in the village of Panchur, in Pauri Garhwal, Uttar Pradesh (now in Uttarakhand) in a Garhwali Rajput family. Adityanath was elected as a Member of Parliament from Gorakhpur "Gorakhpur (Lok Sabha Constituency)") for the first time in 1998 during the 12th Lok Sabha at the age of 26; he was its youngest member at that time. Adityanath was a prominent campaigner for the BJP in the 2017 assembly elections in the state of Uttar Pradesh.

ranked_evidence.snippet: # Shalabh Kumar. **Shalabh "Shalli" Kumar** (Hindi: शलभ कुमार; born 24 December 1948) is a Chicago-based Indian-American industrialist and political donor affiliated with the Republican Party "Republican Party (United States)"). Kumar was a prominent financial backer of Donald Trump's presidential campaign in the 2016 election. He came to the United States as a foreign student when he was 20, to attend Illinois Institute of Technology for his master's degree. In 2014, Kumar worked with the National Republican Congressional Committee (NRCC) to encourage Indian Americans to run for office and get involved politically.*[citation needed*] He was also named Chairman of the Indian American Advisory Council for the House Republican Conference. The story of the Hindu American campaign of 2016 has been written by James Kahrs in a book titled “Ab Ki Baar Trump Sarkar” in which a candidate for President of the United States and the Nominee of one of the two main political parties in the US, spoke in Hindi and proudly pronounced “We Love Hindus”.
